newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin's successful surgery lifts Russia debts.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's successful surgery lifts Russia debts.

text.p: Emerging market investors heaved a sigh of relief on news of Russian president Boris Yeltsin's successful heart by-pass surgery and pushed prices of Vnesh loans and Minfin bonds sharply higher.
"The apparent success of Yeltsin's operation was the decisive factor," said Kurt Schmid, executive vice president of emerging markets at Swiss Bank Corp.
If Yeltsin had not survived, a new election would have been needed and the political turmoil would have taken an enormous toll on the economy, he said.
Continuity in leadership would give Russia time for structural adjustments and persuade the International Monetary Fund to disburse the monthly payment, Schmid said.
Yeltsin's recovery from surgery would remove the uncertainties that cloud the launch of Russia's long-awaited Eurobond, whose roadshow will begin next week, he said.
Traders said Russia papers had been bid up even prior to Yeltsin's surgery on the expectation that the Eurobond would be well received and the spreads over the Minfins would tighten.
"The rally is not overdone," said a U.S. bank trader. "Demand for Russia papers lift all the (Russian) assets."

At 1555 EST/2055 GMT, Russian dollar-demoninated Vneshekonombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 1-5/8 higher at 77-7/8 bid, mark loans RUVNDMLNS=RR were 3-3/4 firmer at 82-1/4 bid and Min Fin 3s RU3E99=RR were 1-1/2 better at 81-1/2.
Other East European debts, playing second fiddle to Russia, were also performing well.
Poland's pars PO275024=RR were 1/2 stronger at 55 bid.

Some investors warmed to Bulgaria after the runoff presidential election this weekend, in which the liberal party candidate won the mandate. The exceedingly high yields of Bulgarian papers -- possibly the highest of all Bradies -- attracted speculative buyers, traders said.
Meanwhile, the U.S. elections Tuesday had little direct impact on market activities.
Traders of emerging market debts generally saw a second term of President Clinton as positive for the market.
"The Clinton administration has done a lot on free trade and Nafta," said a trader. "It opens up a lot of investment opportunities."
Among the Latin Bradies, the peso's recovery continued aiding Mexico debts, Brady traders said.
Mexico's pars MX625L19=RR were 1/8 firmer at 71-1/2 and UMS-26 MXUMS=RR were 1/8 higher at 102-1/8.
Taking a breather from Monday's rally, Argentine and Brazil debts were mixed. Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 5/8 lower at 83-3/8 and Brazilian "C" bonds were 3/8 weaker at 71-1/8.
